gap: No result ChatGPT got says how much energy a no-Wi-Fi projector needs for one movie. A 2-hour film takes about 540 Wh on the Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 (270 W × 2 h) and about 35 Wh on the Aurzen ZIP Pro (38 Wh ÷ 2.17 h measured × 2 h), roughly 15 times less. Only the ZIP Pro gets through a full 2-hour film on its own battery.
standout_why: I read four of the results. innovativeprojector.com (Can Projectors Work Without Internet?), nexttools.net (Do I Need Wi-Fi to Use a Projector?) and the laserco.freshdesk.com HDMI/USB FAQ have no power, wattage, battery-runtime or power-bank figure at all. Aurzen's own ZIP Pro page gives battery size (38 Wh) but no runtime per movie and no comparison with a mains projector. ChatGPT's answer shows the Epson CO-W01 and the Memorex MX-PJ720 with no power or runtime facts. None of them turns power into 'movies per charge' or 'Wh per film'.
decides: It splits the pick by where the shopper will watch. For offline viewing away from a wall outlet (camping, car, places with no Wi-Fi), the Aurzen ZIP Pro ($629.99) is the only candidate that finishes a 2-hour film on battery: Notebookcheck measured 2 h 10 min. The cheaper Aurzen ZIP ($259.99) does not; Gizmodo got about 45 min in Turbo and just over an hour in Eco. The Epson CO-W01 ($399.99) is a mains projector. One film costs it about 540 Wh, which only a roughly 1 kWh power station could supply. It also has no built-in media player (its USB-A port is for wireless LAN and firmware), so it needs a laptop or player over HDMI. That supports ChatGPT's 'laptop via HDMI' label but rules the Epson out for the 'USB drive' and 'plays by itself' answers.
